pages.q: Can I get health insurance if I'm self-employed?
a: Yes. If you're self-employed in Florida, you can buy an individual plan through the Health Insurance Marketplace. You don't need an employer.

Whether you get help paying the premium depends on your estimated household income for the year. For 2027, premium tax credits generally apply between 100% and 400% of the poverty level. The extra subsidies that went above 400% ended after 2025.

Timing matters. Open Enrollment for 2027 runs November 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027, and you need to enroll by December 15 for coverage that starts January 1. If you just lost job-based coverage, you usually have 60 days to enroll through a Special Enrollment Period.
Self-employed people who aren't eligible for an employer plan (their own or a spouse's) may be able to deduct health insurance premiums. Ask your tax professional.

script.hook: Self-employed in Florida and no health insurance? Here's the date that matters.
beats: You don't need an employer: Marketplace plans are open to you.
Help with premiums depends on your 2027 income, and the extra subsidies ended after 2025.
Enroll by Dec 15 for Jan 1 coverage.

pages.q: When can I enroll in health insurance?
a: For 2027 coverage, Open Enrollment runs from November 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027.
Enroll by December 15 for coverage starting January 1. If you enroll between December 16 and January 15, coverage starts February 1 (after you pay the first premium).
Outside Open Enrollment, you need a qualifying life event, like losing other coverage, moving, getting married, having a baby or turning 26. You usually have 60 days after the event to enroll.
You can apply for Medicaid or CHIP at any time of year.

beats: Open Enrollment: Nov 1 - Jan 15.
Dec 15 = coverage on Jan 1.

pages.q: How much does health insurance cost in Florida?
a: There's no single price. Your premium depends on your age, where you live (ZIP code and county), how many people are covered, tobacco use and the plan's metal level.
What you actually pay also depends on income. Premium tax credits lower the monthly premium for households in the eligible range.

Anyone who quotes you a price without asking these questions is guessing. The free check shows your enrollment window and subsidy range. A licensed agent can then pull real plans and prices for your ZIP code.

script.hook: 'How much is health insurance?' The honest answer has 5 parts.
beats: Age, ZIP, household size, tobacco, plan level.
Then income decides how much help you get.

pages.q: Do I qualify for help paying for health insurance?
a: For 2027 coverage, premium tax credits are generally available when household income is between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level, and you don't have access to other qualifying coverage.
The enhanced credits that removed the 400% cap expired at the end of 2025. As of this writing, Congress had not extended them.

Florida has not expanded Medicaid. Many adults below 100% of the poverty level don't qualify for Marketplace credits, and adults without children generally can't get Florida Medicaid. A licensed agent or a free Navigator can review options.
Credits are based on your estimated income for the year and reconciled on your tax return, so update your application if your income changes.

Over that, no credit in 2027.

pages.q: What happens if I lose my employer health insurance?
a: Losing job-based coverage is a qualifying life event. You usually have 60 days to enroll in a Marketplace plan through a Special Enrollment Period, and you can often apply before the coverage ends.
You may also be offered COBRA, which continues your employer plan but usually at the full cost. Compare it with Marketplace options, where premium tax credits may apply depending on income.
If you choose COBRA and later drop it voluntarily outside Open Enrollment, that usually doesn't open a Special Enrollment Period, so decide early.
Don't wait past 60 days: after that, you'd usually have to wait for Open Enrollment.

script.hook: Laid off? You have 60 days. Here's what most people get wrong.
beats: Losing job coverage opens a 60-day window.
COBRA isn't your only option.
Dropping COBRA later usually doesn't reopen the window.

pages.q: Can I get health insurance between jobs?
a: Yes. If you lose job-based coverage, you can usually enroll in a Marketplace plan within 60 days through a Special Enrollment Period. Coverage can begin soon after you pick a plan.
Other routes: COBRA from your former employer, or joining a spouse's or parent's plan (if you're under 26) when their plan allows mid-year changes after your coverage ends.
If your income for the year will be lower because of the gap, update your estimate. You may qualify for more help with premiums.

script.hook: Between jobs and uninsured? Don't wait for your new job's plan.

Under 26? A parent's plan may be an option.

pages.q: How does health insurance work if I'm a 1099 worker?
a: As a 1099 worker you buy your own coverage, usually through the Marketplace. You estimate your household income for the year (for 1099 work, roughly your net profit) and that estimate sets any premium tax credit.
Because 1099 income changes, update your Marketplace application when it does. Credits paid in advance are reconciled when you file taxes, so a big income jump can mean paying some back.
Enroll during Open Enrollment (Nov 1 - Jan 15, by Dec 15 for Jan 1) or within 60 days of losing other coverage.

pages.q: What health insurance options do freelancers have?
a: Freelancers in Florida usually have a few routes: an individual Marketplace plan (with premium tax credits if income is in range), a spouse's or partner's employer plan if eligible, a parent's plan if under 26, or COBRA right after leaving a job.
Marketplace eligibility for help depends on estimated household income. For 2027, help generally stops above 400% of the poverty level.
A licensed agent can compare actual plans and networks for your ZIP code, which is where the real differences show up.

pages.q: ¿Puedo tener seguro médico si trabajo por mi cuenta?
a: Sí. Si trabajas por tu cuenta en Florida, puedes comprar un plan individual en el Mercado de Seguros Médicos. No necesitas un empleador.

Si recibes ayuda con la prima depende de tu ingreso estimado del hogar para el año. Para 2027, el crédito fiscal generalmente aplica entre el 100% y el 400% del nivel de pobreza. Los subsidios extra por encima del 400% terminaron después de 2025.
Rango de subsidio 2027 (100%-400% de las guías de pobreza 2026): 1 persona $15,960-$63,840 · 2 personas $21,640-$86,560 · 3 personas $27,320-$109,280 · 4 personas $33,000-$132,000.

La fecha importa: la Inscripción Abierta para 2027 va del 1 de noviembre de 2026 al 15 de enero de 2027, y debes inscribirte antes del 15 de diciembre para cobertura desde el 1 de enero. Si acabas de perder la cobertura de un trabajo, normalmente tienes 60 días.
Si trabajas por tu cuenta y no tienes acceso a un plan de empleador (tuyo o de tu pareja), podrías deducir las primas. Pregúntale a tu contador.

beats: No necesitas un empleador: el Mercado está abierto para ti.

Inscríbete antes del 15 de diciembre para el 1 de enero.

pages.q: ¿Cuándo me puedo inscribir en un seguro médico?

Inscríbete antes del 15 de diciembre para que la cobertura empiece el 1 de enero. Si te inscribes entre el 16 de diciembre y el 15 de enero, empieza el 1 de febrero (después de pagar la primera prima).
Fuera de esas fechas necesitas un evento de vida que califique, como perder otra cobertura, mudarte, casarte, tener un bebé o cumplir 26. Normalmente tienes 60 días después del evento.
Puedes solicitar Medicaid o CHIP en cualquier momento del año.

pages.q: ¿Cuánto cuesta un seguro médico en Florida?
a: No hay un solo precio. La prima depende de tu edad, dónde vives (código postal y condado), cuántas personas se cubren, si usas tabaco y el nivel del plan.
Lo que pagas también depende del ingreso: el crédito fiscal baja la prima mensual para los hogares en el rango que califica.
Rango de subsidio 2027 (100%-400% de las guías de pobreza 2026): 1 persona $15,960-$63,840 · 2 personas $21,640-$86,560 · 3 personas $27,320-$109,280 · 4 personas $33,000-$132,000.

Si alguien te da un precio sin hacerte estas preguntas, está adivinando. El chequeo gratis te muestra tu periodo de inscripción y tu rango de subsidio. Después, un agente con licencia puede buscar planes y precios reales para tu código postal.

Rango de subsidio 2027 (100%-400% de las guías de pobreza 2026): 1 persona $15,960-$63,840 · 2 personas $21,640-$86,560 · 3 personas $27,320-$109,280 · 4 personas $33,000-$132,000.

pages.q: Laid off in Florida? Your work life insurance usually ends too, and you have 31 days to act
a: Most life insurance through work is group coverage. When the job ends, that coverage usually ends too, often on your last day or at the end of that month. Your HR or benefits packet has the exact date.

Florida law (section 627.566) gives you the right to convert group life coverage into an individual policy if you apply within 31 days after it ends, without a health exam. The new policy can't be for more than the coverage you lost.

Converting isn't always the best deal. A converted policy is usually permanent-type coverage priced at your current age, so it can cost much more than a new term policy. If you're healthy, a new term policy is often cheaper; if you have health issues, the no-exam conversion can be the safer route. Some employers also offer 'portability' that keeps term coverage at group rates - ask HR before the 31 days run out.

If the whole company shut down and the group policy itself ended, Florida law (section 627.567) only guarantees conversion if you were insured for at least 5 years, and the insurer can limit it to $10,000. In a closure, plan on replacing the coverage yourself.

What to do this week: find your coverage amount and end date, write down your family's monthly expenses and debts, and compare conversion with a new policy before day 31. A licensed life insurance agent can do that comparison with you; their help doesn't cost you anything.

pages.q: ¿Te despidieron en Florida? El seguro de vida del trabajo normalmente también termina, y tienes 31 días
a: La mayoría de los seguros de vida del trabajo son de grupo. Cuando termina el empleo, esa cobertura normalmente termina también, muchas veces el último día o al final de ese mes. Tu paquete de beneficios o Recursos Humanos tiene la fecha exacta.

La ley de Florida (sección 627.566) te da el derecho de convertir el seguro de vida de grupo en una póliza individual si lo solicitas dentro de los 31 días después de que termina, sin examen médico. La póliza nueva no puede ser por más de la cobertura que perdiste.

Convertir no siempre es lo más barato. La póliza convertida normalmente es de tipo permanente y se cobra según tu edad actual, así que puede costar mucho más que una póliza a término nueva. Si estás saludable, una póliza a término nueva suele salir más barata; si tienes problemas de salud, la conversión sin examen puede ser la opción más segura. Algunos empleadores también ofrecen 'portabilidad', que mantiene la cobertura a término con tarifas de grupo; pregunta a Recursos Humanos antes de que pasen los 31 días.

Si la empresa cerró por completo y la póliza de grupo terminó, la ley de Florida (sección 627.567) solo garantiza la conversión si estuviste asegurado al menos 5 años, y la aseguradora puede limitarla a $10,000. Si tu empresa cerró, piensa en reemplazar la cobertura por tu cuenta.

Qué hacer esta semana: busca tu monto de cobertura y la fecha en que termina, apunta los gastos mensuales y deudas de tu familia, y compara la conversión con una póliza nueva antes del día 31. Un agente de seguros de vida con licencia puede hacer esa comparación contigo, sin costo para ti.

pages.q: Leaving the military in Florida? Your SGLI life insurance has two deadlines: 120 days and 240 days
a: SGLI, the group life insurance you have on active duty, doesn't follow you into civilian life on its own. The VA gives you options, and each one has a clock that starts the day you separate.

240 days (about 8 months): if you apply for Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) within 240 days of separation, the VA says it won't consider your health conditions when deciding whether you're eligible. After 240 days you have to submit evidence of good health. The outside limit is 1 year and 120 days after you leave service, and you need to have had SGLI while on active duty of 31 days or more. VGLI covers $10,000 to $500,000, based on the SGLI coverage you had when you left.

120 days (about 4 months): the VA also says you can convert SGLI into a permanent policy from a private company if you apply within 120 days of separation, and you don't have to prove good health to get standard premium rates.

How they differ: VGLI is term coverage. Its premiums depend on your age bracket and rise as you move into older brackets. A permanent private policy usually costs more at the start, but the price stays the same for as long as you keep it. Neither is automatically better; it depends on your health, your budget and how long your family needs the coverage. A new policy bought on the open market is a third option, and it is the one where health questions matter most, so it is worth looking at while you're still within the no-health-review windows.

What to do this week: find your separation date and write both deadlines on the calendar (120 days and 240 days from that date), find your SGLI amount on your last Leave and Earnings Statement, and list what your family would need to cover (mortgage, rent, childcare, debts). A licensed life insurance agent can walk through the options with you at no cost to you; the VA also answers questions directly.
We are not affiliated with the VA, the Department of Defense or TRICARE. Check your own dates with your separation paperwork, milConnect or the VA.

pages.q: Leaving the military in Florida? What happens to your TRICARE and your family's health coverage
a: Military health coverage ends on a date, and the options that follow have their own deadlines. Which ones apply to you depends on how you separate, so check your own paperwork.

TRICARE: eligibility for you and your family generally ends when you separate. TRICARE says the Transitional Assistance Management Program (TAMP) provides 180 days of health care benefits after regular TRICARE benefits end, with no premiums, for certain groups, such as people involuntarily separating under honorable conditions, some Guard and Reserve members who served more than 30 consecutive days on a contingency mission, and a few others. TAMP is not for everyone: your eligibility is set by your service and shows in DEERS (check milConnect).

After TAMP, or if you don't qualify for it: the Continued Health Care Benefit Program (CHCBP) is premium-based continuation coverage run by Humana Military. For most separating service members it lasts up to 18 months, and TRICARE's general rule is that you must apply within 60 days of losing TRICARE coverage (60 days of losing TAMP, if you had it). Missing that deadline can close the door, so put the date on a calendar.

Marketplace: TRICARE counts as minimum essential coverage under federal law (26 U.S.C. 5000A), and losing minimum essential coverage is generally a reason for a Special Enrollment Period, which can start up to 60 days before coverage ends and runs for 60 days after. HealthCare.gov's own page lists examples such as job-based coverage but doesn't name TRICARE, so confirm your window with HealthCare.gov or a licensed agent before relying on it. Enrolling before your coverage ends avoids a gap.
VA health care is for the veteran, and generally doesn't cover a spouse or children. If you have family members, plan their coverage separately.

What to do this week: find your separation date and your TAMP status in milConnect, write down the date 60 days before TRICARE/TAMP ends, list your family's doctors and prescriptions, and compare options before that date. A licensed agent can check which Marketplace plans include your doctors and medicines at no cost to you, because agents are paid by the insurance companies.
We are not affiliated with the VA, the Department of Defense or TRICARE. Check your own dates with your separation paperwork, milConnect or the VA.

pages.q: Florida health plans in 2027: who's leaving, how much prices are going up, and what to do
a: Cigna (Cigna Health & Life and Cigna HMO) is the one insurer confirmed to be leaving Florida's individual Marketplace for 2027. If your plan is with Cigna, it ends December 31, 2026, and you should get a letter about it by November 1. Two other names you may have heard: Ambetter's parent company, Centene, is moving members of its Sunshine State Health Plan entity to an Ambetter plan (the brand continues in Florida, but the plan, network and price can change), and Molina has said it is cutting back its marketplace states without naming them, so a Molina member should wait for a letter before assuming anything.

What happens if you do nothing: HealthCare.gov says that if your company isn't offering plans next year, it will re-enroll you in a plan with a different insurance company. You keep coverage, but that plan may not include your doctors or your medicines, and many people only find out at their first appointment or pharmacy visit in January. Sunshine State Health Plan members are expected to move to Ambetter (same parent company).

Bought your plan directly from the insurance company instead of HealthCare.gov? Then nobody moves you automatically: when the company leaves, that plan simply ends on December 31. Losing it opens a Special Enrollment Period from 60 days before to 60 days after it ends, but don't wait - choose by December 15 so there's no gap on January 1.

Prices: Florida insurers asked for an average increase of about 15.9% for 2027, with requests from about 4% to 39% depending on the company. Final 2027 prices show up on HealthCare.gov when Open Enrollment opens November 1.

Help paying premiums: the extra subsidies that ran from 2021 to 2025 ended. Under current law, premium tax credits for 2027 generally apply when household income is between 100% and 400% of the poverty level: $15,960 to $63,840 for one person, $33,000 to $132,000 for a family of four.
Deadlines: Open Enrollment runs November 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027. Choose a plan by December 15 for coverage that starts January 1.

What to do now: keep the letter, write down your doctors and prescriptions, and compare 2027 plans in November, before December 15. A licensed agent can check which plans include your doctors and medicines. Licensed agents are paid by the insurance companies, so their help doesn't cost you anything.

beats: Cigna plans end Dec 31.

Pick a new plan by Dec 15 so there's no gap on Jan 1.

pages.q: Seguro médico en Florida 2027: qué compañías se van, cuánto suben los precios y qué hacer
a: Cigna (Cigna Health & Life y Cigna HMO) es la única aseguradora confirmada que sale del Mercado individual de Florida en 2027. Si tu plan es con Cigna, termina el 31 de diciembre de 2026 y debes recibir una carta antes del 1 de noviembre. Otros nombres que quizás hayas oído: Centene, la empresa matriz de Ambetter, pasa a los miembros de su entidad Sunshine State Health Plan a un plan Ambetter (la marca sigue en Florida, pero el plan, la red y el precio pueden cambiar), y Molina dijo que reducirá sus estados en el Mercado sin nombrarlos; si tienes Molina, espera tu carta antes de suponer algo.

Qué pasa si no haces nada: CuidadoDeSalud.gov dice que si tu compañía no ofrece planes el próximo año, te inscribirá en un plan de otra compañía de seguros. Sigues con cobertura, pero ese plan puede no incluir a tus médicos ni tus medicinas, y mucha gente se entera en enero, en su primera cita o en la farmacia. pages.q: Laid off in Florida? Your 60-day health coverage plan (COBRA vs Marketplace)
a: Losing job-based health coverage opens a Special Enrollment Period: you usually have 60 days from the day your coverage ends to enroll in a Marketplace plan.

COBRA lets you keep your employer's plan, but you usually pay the full cost plus up to 2%, which is often far more than you paid as an employee. You generally have 60 days to elect COBRA, and coverage is retroactive if you elect and pay.

Important: if you take COBRA and later drop it on purpose, that does not open a new Special Enrollment Period. Compare before you decide; you can still switch to a Marketplace plan during Open Enrollment (November 1 to January 15).

Help paying premiums: the extra subsidies that ran from 2021 to 2025 ended. Under current law, premium tax credits for 2027 generally apply when household income is between 100% and 400% of the poverty level: $15,960 to $63,840 for one person, $33,000 to $132,000 for a family of four.

What to do now: find the date your employer coverage ends, gather your severance and expected income for the rest of the year, and compare COBRA's price with Marketplace plans before day 60. A licensed agent can run that comparison with you at no cost to you.

COBRA te deja mantener el plan de tu empleador, pero normalmente pagas el costo completo más hasta un 2%, que suele ser mucho más de lo que pagabas como empleado. Por lo general tienes 60 días para elegir COBRA, y la cobertura es retroactiva si la eliges y pagas.

Importante: si tomas COBRA y después la dejas por tu cuenta, eso no abre un nuevo Periodo Especial de Inscripción. Compara antes de decidir; igual puedes cambiarte a un plan del Mercado en la Inscripción Abierta (del 1 de noviembre al 15 de enero).

Qué hacer ahora: averigua la fecha en que termina tu seguro del trabajo, junta tu liquidación y tu ingreso esperado para el resto del año, y compara el precio de COBRA con los planes del Mercado antes del día 60. Un agente con licencia puede hacer esa comparación contigo sin costo para ti.

Missed January 15? Whether it applies when you were already moved to a new plan depends on your case - a licensed agent can check it with you. Acting before January 15 is the safe route.
Before you switch, check three things in any plan: your doctors, your medicines and the hospital you use.
A licensed agent can check which 2027 plans include your doctors and medicines and help you switch before January 15. Their help doesn't cost you anything.

This is different from dropping COBRA early or not paying: stopping COBRA on purpose, or losing it for non-payment, does not open a Special Enrollment Period.
If you were laid off in spring 2025 and kept COBRA, your 18 months end in fall 2026 or early 2027, close to Open Enrollment (November 1 to January 15).

pages.q: ¿Sales del ejército en Florida? Qué pasa con TRICARE y con la cobertura de tu familia
a: La cobertura médica militar termina en una fecha, y las opciones que siguen tienen sus propios plazos. Cuáles te aplican depende de cómo te separes, así que revisa tus propios documentos.

TRICARE: la elegibilidad para ti y tu familia por lo general termina cuando te separas. TRICARE explica que el Programa de Gestión de Asistencia de Transición (TAMP) da 180 días de beneficios médicos después de que terminan los beneficios regulares de TRICARE, sin primas, para ciertos grupos, como personas que se separan de forma involuntaria con condiciones honorables, algunos miembros de la Guardia y la Reserva que sirvieron más de 30 días consecutivos en una misión de contingencia, y algunos otros casos. TAMP no es para todos: tu elegibilidad la fija tu rama y aparece en DEERS (revisa milConnect).

Después de TAMP, o si no calificas: el Programa de Cobertura Médica Continua (CHCBP) es una cobertura de continuación con primas administrada por Humana Military. Para la mayoría de los militares que se separan dura hasta 18 meses, y la regla general de TRICARE es que debes solicitarla dentro de los 60 días siguientes a la pérdida de la cobertura de TRICARE (60 días desde que termina TAMP, si lo tuviste). Perder ese plazo puede cerrar la puerta, así que anota la fecha.

Mercado: TRICARE cuenta como cobertura mínima esencial bajo la ley federal (26 U.S.C. 5000A), y perder la cobertura mínima esencial generalmente es motivo de un Periodo Especial de Inscripción, que puede empezar hasta 60 días antes de que termine la cobertura y dura 60 días después. La página de HealthCare.gov da ejemplos como la cobertura del trabajo, pero no menciona TRICARE, así que confirma tu ventana con HealthCare.gov o con un agente con licencia antes de confiar en ella. Inscribirte antes de que termine tu cobertura evita un hueco.
La atención médica de VA es para el veterano y por lo general no cubre a cónyuge ni hijos. Si tienes familia, planea su cobertura por separado.

Qué hacer esta semana: busca tu fecha de separación y tu estatus de TAMP en milConnect, anota la fecha 60 días antes de que termine TRICARE/TAMP, haz una lista de los médicos y medicamentos de tu familia, y compara opciones antes de esa fecha. Un agente con licencia puede revisar sin costo para ti qué planes del Mercado incluyen a tus médicos y medicamentos, porque a los agentes los pagan las aseguradoras.
No estamos afiliados con el VA, el Departamento de Defensa ni TRICARE. Confirma tus fechas con tus documentos de separación, milConnect o el VA.

script.hook: ¿Sales del ejército? La cobertura médica de tu familia tiene un plazo que muchos descubren demasiado tarde.
beats: TRICARE termina cuando te separas. TAMP da 180 días más a algunos grupos.
CHCBP es cobertura de continuación con primas: solicítala dentro de 60 días.
Un plan del Mercado es la otra opción; inscribirte antes de que termine tu cobertura evita un hueco.

pages.q: ¿Sales del ejército en Florida? Tu seguro de vida SGLI tiene dos plazos: 120 días y 240 días
a: SGLI, el seguro de vida grupal que tienes en servicio activo, no te sigue a la vida civil por sí solo. El VA te da opciones y cada una tiene un reloj que empieza el día que te separas.

240 días (unos 8 meses): si solicitas el Seguro de Vida Grupal para Veteranos (VGLI) dentro de los 240 días siguientes a la separación, el VA indica que no tomará en cuenta tus condiciones de salud para decidir si calificas. Después de 240 días tienes que presentar prueba de buena salud. El límite máximo es 1 año y 120 días después de dejar el servicio, y necesitas haber tenido SGLI en servicio activo por 31 días o más. VGLI cubre de $10,000 a $500,000, según la cobertura de SGLI que tenías al salir.

120 días (unos 4 meses): el VA también indica que puedes convertir SGLI en una póliza permanente de una compañía privada si solicitas dentro de los 120 días siguientes a la separación, y no tienes que probar buena salud para obtener las tarifas estándar.

En qué se diferencian: VGLI es cobertura a término. Sus primas dependen de tu grupo de edad y suben cuando pasas a grupos mayores. Una póliza permanente privada suele costar más al inicio, pero el precio se mantiene igual mientras la conserves. Ninguna es automáticamente mejor; depende de tu salud, tu presupuesto y cuánto tiempo tu familia necesita la cobertura. Una póliza nueva comprada en el mercado abierto es una tercera opción, y es la que más depende de las preguntas de salud, así que vale la pena revisarla mientras sigues dentro de las ventanas sin revisión de salud.

Qué hacer esta semana: busca tu fecha de separación y anota los dos plazos en el calendario (120 días y 240 días desde esa fecha), encuentra el monto de tu SGLI en tu último Estado de Licencia y Haberes (LES), y haz una lista de lo que tu familia necesitaría cubrir (hipoteca, renta, cuidado de niños, deudas). Un agente de seguros de vida con licencia puede revisar las opciones contigo sin costo para ti; el VA también responde preguntas directamente.
No estamos afiliados con el VA, el Departamento de Defensa ni TRICARE. Confirma tus fechas con tus documentos de separación, milConnect o el VA.

script.hook: ¿Sales del ejército? Tu SGLI tiene dos fechas límite, y una es mucho más corta de lo que crees.
beats: 240 días: VGLI sin revisar tu salud.
120 días: conversión a póliza permanente sin prueba de salud.
Anota ambas fechas el día que te separes.
